messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High rate of container restarts on gpu-pool-3; 5xxs increasing. Possible OOMs during prefill. Paging oncall (alex_sre).
alex_sre: I’m on it. grabbing logs and lock screen. where is the impact? any customer-facing errors yet?
mira_runtime: seeing repeated ContainerExited from runtime on node g3-17. Crash log shows CUDA OOM during prefill for long-context requests.
raj_infra: nodes are flapping 3/25 in that pool. kube shows evictions + restarts. No node reboots yet.
alex_sre: paste recent logs from one container:
```
2026-03-17T12:34:56Z ERROR runtime: prefill failed: CUDA error: out of memory
stack: /opt/runtime/serve/prefill.go:142
container: redwood-runtime-7bb9c9
OOM alloc request 24.5GB > free 1.2GB
killed by OOM killer, pid 4123, signal 9
```
joan_cs: Customer Success ping — one enterprise customer reported "server busy" and 503s on long-document summarization. They flagged a production job at 12:30 UTC.
sam_pm: queued an incident update to the status page draft. Need impact estimate.
alex_sre: quick mitigation idea: enable prefill token cap on frontier routing for the GPU pool (trim inputs > 32k tokens to 32k), and set fallback to cpu-coldmodel for oversized requests. Will apply as a live rule if we can.
mira_runtime: +1 on prefill cap. Also can disable continuous KV cache for new sessions in this pool (reduces memory footprint) — cheap toggle.
raj_infra: I can patch the pool autoscaler to avoid burst scheduling to these nodes and signal drain heavy pods to spare room. Doing careful drains though to avoid extra restarts.
alex_sre: Live-change plan:
- Step 1 (T+3m): Add routing rule: if prompt_tokens > 32768 -> route to cpu-coldmodel-fallback
- Step 2 (T+5m): Set prefill_limit=32768 for gpu-pool-3
- Step 3 (T+7m): disable kv-cache-for-new-sessions on gpu-pool-3
- Step 4 (T+10m): monitor error rate, revert if regressions
Anyone object?
mira_runtime: executing steps 1 and 2 now. pushing rule via console -> rollout: canary 10% -> 100% in 30s.
deploy-bot: rule rollout started: rule-id r-9b1c; canary=10%; expected prop delay ~30s.
alex_sre: seeing first canary traffic. error rates for pool dropping from 4.5% -> 2.1% for prefill path.
joan_cs: updated the customer with "We are actively mitigating OOMs by routing very large requests to a fallback model; we expect recovery within 20m." They replied thanks, asked about data residency (they're okay).
sam_pm: added to status: "partial impact for long-context workloads in us-west; mitigation underway". Will post update at 12:55 UTC.
mira_runtime: after full rollout, container restarts reduced to 0 in last 5m. node memory pressure lowered. Monitoring shows latency on fallback path increased but within SLA.
alex_sre: next steps: create a post-incident ticket to instrument prefill token distribution and add a hard cap in serving runtime, evaluate quantization for coldmodel, and consider more graceful prefill trimming for user UX.
raj_infra: I'll keep the pool in gentle drain-proof mode for 30m to ensure stability. Will roll back autoscaler changes after.
joan_cs: I'll follow up with affected customer with root-cause summary after incident postmortem.
sam_pm: thanks all — marking this thread as incident in progress. Will update timeline in incident doc.
alex_sre: closing pager for now, leaving followup actions assigned. :white_check_mark:
